```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE
)
```

## Introduction

This project examines McDonald's ice cream machine reliability across the United States using monthly data from November 2025 to October 2026. The analysis focuses on data quality, machine brokenness, temporal changes, and geographic differences in machine performance.

## Problem 1 - Data Import

```{r}
snapshot_files =
  list.files(
    path = "data",
    pattern = "^mcbroken_.*\\.csv$",
    full.names = TRUE
  )

mcbroken_df =
  read_csv(
    snapshot_files,
    na = c("", "NA"),
    show_col_types = FALSE
  )

store_info_df =
  read_csv(
    "data/store_info.csv",
    show_col_types = FALSE
  )

state_regions_df =
  read_csv(
    "data/state_regions.csv",
    show_col_types = FALSE
  )
```



```{r}
mcbroken_df =
  mcbroken_df |>
  mutate(
    month = as.Date(str_sub(month, 1, 10))
  ) |>
  left_join(store_info_df, by = "store_id") |>
  left_join(state_regions_df, by = "state") |>
  relocate(
    month, store_id, state, region,
    city, street, longitude, latitude
  )
```

```{r}
data_summary_df =
  mcbroken_df |>
  summarize(
    n_observations = n(),
    n_months = n_distinct(month),
    n_stores = n_distinct(store_id),
    missing_status = sum(
      is.na(active) & is.na(broken)
    )
  )

data_summary_df |>
  knitr::kable()
```

The 12 monthly datasets were combined, and the month variable was converted to a Date. Store information and geographic regions were added using `left_join()`. Missing machine statuses were retained for later investigation.

The resulting dataset contains `r pull(data_summary_df, n_observations)` observations from `r pull(data_summary_df, n_months)` months and `r pull(data_summary_df, n_stores)` unique stores. Important variables include store ID, month, active status, broken status, state, region, and geographic coordinates.

Store counts by state
```{r}
store_counts_df = 
  mcbroken_df |> 
  group_by(state) |> 
  summarize(
    n_stores = n_distinct(store_id),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |> 
  arrange(desc(n_stores))

store_counts_df |>
  summarize(total_stores = sum(n_stores)) |>
  knitr::kable()

store_counts_df |> 
  filter(
    n_stores == max(n_stores) | n_stores == min(n_stores)
  ) |> 
  knitr::kable()
```
```{r}
brokenness_df = 
  mcbroken_df |> 
  filter(active == T) |> 
  summarize(
    n_active = n(),
    n_broken = sum(broken, na.rm = T),
    broken_rate = mean(broken, na.rm = T)
  )

brokenness_df |> 
  knitr::kable(digits = 4)
```

The dataset contains 13,792 stores. Texas has the most (1,269), while Vermont has the fewest (25) among U.S. states. Including territories, the Northern Mariana Islands has the fewest (2). Among active machine observations, the brokenness rate was 14.44% (21,826/151,113).

## Problem 2 - Exploratory Analysis

```{r}
store_summary_df = 
  mcbroken_df |>  
  group_by(store_id, state, city, street, latitude, longitude) |>
  summarize(
    n_obs = n(),
    n_known = sum(!is.na(active)),
    n_active = sum(active == T, na.rm = T),
    n_inactive = sum(active == F, na.rm = T),
    n_broken = sum(broken == T, na.rm = T),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    inactive_rate = ifelse(
      n_known > 0, n_inactive / n_known, NA_real_
    ),
    broken_rate = ifelse(
      n_active > 0, n_broken / n_active, NA_real_
    )
  )

```

Store with few observations
```{r}
store_summary_df |> 
  filter(n_obs < 9) |> 
  summarize(
    n_stores = n(),
    one_observation = sum(n_obs == 1)
  ) |> 
  knitr::kable()

store_summary_df |>
  filter(n_obs < 9) |>
  arrange(n_obs, store_id) |>
  slice_head(n = 10) |>
  select(store_id, state, city, n_obs) |>
  knitr::kable()
```


```{r}
# High inactivity
store_summary_df |>
  filter(n_obs >= 9, n_known > 0) |>
  arrange(desc(inactive_rate)) |>
  select(store_id, state, city, street,
         n_obs, n_inactive, n_known, inactive_rate) |>
  slice_head(n = 6) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)

# High brokenness filter
store_summary_df |>
  filter(n_obs >= 9, n_active >= 9) |>
  arrange(desc(broken_rate), desc(n_active)) |>
  select(store_id, state, city, street,
         n_obs, n_active, n_broken, broken_rate) |>
  slice_head(n = 10) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)

```

```{r}
# Geographic coordinates
coordinate_outliers_df =
  store_summary_df |>
  filter(
    !(state %in% c("AK", "HI", "GU", "MP")),
    !between(latitude, 24, 50) |
      !between(longitude, -125, -66)
  ) |>
  select(store_id, state, city, street,
         latitude, longitude)

coordinate_outliers_df |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)

```

Among 13,792 stores, 239 have fewer than nine observations, including 40 observed only once.Among stores with at least nine observations, the highest inactivity rate was 90% in Windsor Locks, CT, while several stores reported 100% brokenness across 12 active observations. A geographic check identified three implausible mainland coordinates, suggesting potential data-quality issues. 

```{r}
# Nearest store
mailman_lat = 40.8421
mailman_lon = -73.9423

nearest_store_df =
  store_summary_df |>
  filter(!is.na(latitude), !is.na(longitude)) |>
  mutate(
    distance_km = 111.2 * sqrt(
      (latitude - mailman_lat)^2 +
      ((longitude - mailman_lon) *
         cos(mailman_lat * pi / 180))^2
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(distance_km) |>
  slice_head(n = 1)

nearest_store_df |>
  select(store_id, state, city, street, distance_km,
         n_obs, n_active, n_broken, broken_rate) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

```{r}
# Nearest store history
mcbroken_df |>
  filter(store_id == nearest_store_df$store_id[1]) |>
  arrange(month) |>
  mutate(
    status = case_when(
      is.na(active) | is.na(broken) ~ "Unknown",
      active == FALSE ~ "Inactive",
      broken == TRUE ~ "Broken",
      TRUE ~ "Working"
    )
  ) |>
  select(month,store_id, status) |>
  knitr::kable()
```


```{r}
# Highest brokenness in NYC
nyc_store_df =
  store_summary_df |>
  filter(
    state == "NY",
    between(latitude, 40.49, 40.92),
    between(longitude, -74.26, -73.70),
    !(city %in% c(
      "Yonkers", "Mount Vernon", "New Rochelle",
      "Valley Stream", "Lawrence"
    ))
  )

nyc_top_df =
  nyc_store_df |>
  filter(n_active > 0) |>
  filter(
    broken_rate == max(broken_rate, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(n_active))

nyc_top_df |>
  select(store_id, city, street, n_active,
         n_broken, broken_rate) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

The closest store to Mailman is at 4040 Broadway, with a brokenness rate of 8.33% (1/12), occurring in September 2026. Five NYC stores reported 100% brokenness, although one had only three active observations.


```{r}
# Monthly status transitions
transition_df =
  mcbroken_df |>
  arrange(store_id, month) |>
  group_by(store_id) |>
  mutate(
    previous_month = lag(month),
    previous_active = lag(active),
    previous_broken = lag(broken)
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(
    month == previous_month + lubridate::period(months = 1),    
    active == TRUE,
    previous_active == TRUE,
    !is.na(broken),
    !is.na(previous_broken)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    previous_status = if_else(
      previous_broken, "Broken", "Working"
    ),
    current_status = if_else(
      broken, "Broken", "Working"
    )
  ) |>
  count(previous_status, current_status) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = current_status,
    values_from = n,
    values_fill = 0
  ) |>
  mutate(
    previous_status = factor(
      previous_status,
      levels = c("Working", "Broken")
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(previous_status) |>
  select(previous_status, Working, Broken)

transition_df |>
  knitr::kable()
```

Among previously working machines, 101,446 remained working and 8,176 became broken. Among previously broken machines, 7,918 were repaired, while 10,521 remained broken. These results suggest that machine failures often persist across monthly snapshots.

```{r}
# Regional brokenness
region_month_df =
  mcbroken_df |>
  filter(active == TRUE, !is.na(broken)) |>
  group_by(region, month) |>
  summarize(
    broken_rate = 100 * mean(broken),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    month = format(month, "%b %y")
  ) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = month,
    values_from = broken_rate
  ) |>
  arrange(region)

region_month_df |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 1,
    caption = "Monthly brokenness rates (%) by region"
  )
```

Brokenness rates varied across regions and months, with Alaska reaching 47.8% in August 2026, while the Ohio Valley remained relatively stable at approximately 12–15%.

## Problem 3

```{r, fig.width=8, fig.height=10}
# Brokenness by state
state_month_df =
  mcbroken_df |>
  filter(active == TRUE, !is.na(broken)) |>
  group_by(state, month) |>
  summarize(
    broken_rate = mean(broken),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    month_label = factor(
      format(month, "%b %y"),
      levels = format(
        sort(unique(mcbroken_df$month)),
        "%b %y"
      )
    )
  )

state_month_df |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = month_label,
    y = state,
    fill = broken_rate
  )) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    labels = scales::percent_format(),
    name = "Brokenness"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly Brokenness Rate by State",
    x = "Month",
    y = "State"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45, hjust = 1
    ),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )
```
Brokenness rates were generally low across most states and months, although some states experienced substantial monthly spikes, indicating temporal variation. 

```{r,fig.width=9, fig.height=12, out.width="100%"}
store_avg_df =
  mcbroken_df |>
  group_by(
    store_id, state, city, street,
    latitude, longitude
  ) |>
  summarize(
    n_active = sum(active == TRUE, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_broken = mean(
      broken[active == TRUE], na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    avg_broken = if_else(
      is.nan(avg_broken),
      NA_real_,
      avg_broken
    )
  )

# boxplot
store_avg_df |>
  filter(!is.na(avg_broken)) |>
  mutate(
    state = fct_reorder(
      state, avg_broken, .fun = mean
    )
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = state,
    y = avg_broken
  )) +
  geom_boxplot(
    fill = "lightblue",
    outlier.alpha = 0.15,
    outlier.size = 0.6
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::percent_format()
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Store-Level Brokenness by State",
    x = "State",
    y = "Average Brokenness Rate"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Store-level brokenness rates varied considerably within states. Alaska and Hawaii showed relatively high average brokenness, while many states had lower medians but some stores with exceptionally high rates.

```{r,fig.width=15, fig.height=6, out.width="100%"}
# geographic coordinates
library(patchwork)

continental_df =
  store_avg_df |>
  filter(
    !(state %in% c("AK", "HI", "GU", "MP")),
    between(latitude, 24, 50),
    between(longitude, -125, -66)
  )

nyc_plot_df =
  store_avg_df |>
  semi_join(
    nyc_store_df |> select(store_id),
    by = "store_id"
  )

# two panel plots
us_plot =
  continental_df |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = longitude,
    y = latitude,
    color = avg_broken
  )) +
  geom_point(size = 0.6, alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(
    limits = c(0, 1),
    labels = scales::percent_format(),
    na.value = "grey70",
    name = "Brokenness"
  ) +
  coord_quickmap() +
  labs(
    title = "Contiguous United States",
    x = "Longitude",
    y = "Latitude"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

nyc_plot =
  nyc_plot_df |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = longitude,
    y = latitude,
    color = avg_broken
  )) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(
    limits = c(0, 1),
    labels = scales::percent_format(),
    na.value = "grey70",
    name = "Brokenness"
  ) +
  coord_quickmap() +
  labs(
    title = "New York City",
    x = "Longitude",
    y = "Latitude"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

(us_plot | nyc_plot) +
  plot_layout(
    widths = c(1.4, 1),
    guides = "collect"
  ) &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Stores were more densely concentrated in the eastern United States and major urban areas. Within NYC, brokenness rates varied across nearby stores, suggesting no clear uniform geographic pattern.
